transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

I can’t stop obsessing over how terrible I look in photos and at events, and it’s making me want to avoid people altogether. It has gotten so bad lately that I'm just dreading any kind of social gathering.

When you worry about how you look, is it mainly because you fear other people will judge or embarrass you in social situations, or because you believe there is a specific flaw or defect in your appearance that others may not notice?

It’s really a combination of both, but it starts with me seeing these specific, awful flaws in how saggy and crooked my face, jawline, and neck look under bright lights. I constantly replay those images in my head, convinced everyone else is noticing how terrible I look and judging me, even though my husband and sister swear they don't see what I'm talking about.
Do you believe these flaws are definitely real and obvious to others, or do you think there is a chance they might be exaggerated by your mind?

I feel absolutely convinced that these flaws are completely real and obvious to everyone. Even though my family tries to reassure me and says they don't see it, I just can't believe it's in my head when my saggy jawline and crooked face look so glaringly obvious under the lights. I truly feel like everyone else must be noticing it and judging me for it.
Do you avoid social situations mainly because you fear being judged or embarrassed, or because you are focused on fixing or hiding the specific flaws in your appearance?

It is definitely a combination of both. I spend hours before an event in front of the mirror adjusting my hair and glasses or smoothing my skin to try and hide my saggy, crooked neck and jawline. But it becomes so exhausting and distressing that I ultimately choose to stay home just to avoid the shame of others noticing and judging me.

When you are with other people, is your main fear that they will judge you because of your appearance, or do you also worry a lot about being embarrassed in general, even when your appearance is not the focus?

My fear is absolutely about my appearance. I get sick with embarrassment because I am convinced everyone is noticing and judging my saggy jawline, crooked face, and wrinkles under the lights. If it weren't for how terrible I look, I wouldn't have this intense dread or want to avoid people at all.

Do you spend a lot of time checking mirrors, comparing your appearance to others, or trying to hide/fix the specific features you dislike? Or is the main problem simply fear of being judged in social situations even when you are not focused on your appearance?

Yes, I spend hours standing inches from the mirror tilting my head, smoothing my skin, and changing my hair and glasses. I even take dozens of selfies just to zoom in on every wrinkle, and then I constantly ask my husband or sister if my face looks lopsided or awful. It is definitely an obsession with these specific features rather than just a general fear of social situations.
When you avoid social situations, is it mainly because you fear being judged or embarrassed in general, or because you are focused on hiding or fixing the specific flaws you see in your appearance?

My avoidance is completely tied to trying to hide these specific flaws in my appearance. I spend hours adjusting my hair, glasses, and tilting my head to cover up my saggy, crooked neck and jawline, but I still end up staying home because I can't bear the thought of people seeing these flaws under bright lights or in photos. I am just too ashamed to let anyone see me like this.
Before the appearance concerns started, did you already fear social situations because of being judged, embarrassed, or saying the wrong thing, even when you were not worried about how you looked?

No, not at all; before this started, I was actually very active in my community and loved singing in the choir, volunteering for the theater crew, and attending bridge club. This fear of being around people is completely new to me and is entirely because of how awful I think I look now.
Do you ever worry that other people are watching or judging you mainly because of how you look, or is your fear only about specific flaws in your appearance rather than social situations in general?

My fear is entirely driven by the specific flaws I see in my face, like my saggy jawline and crooked neck under the lights. I'm constantly convinced that everyone is staring at and judging these exact areas, even though my family insists they don't see anything wrong. It's this intense shame about my appearance—and nothing else—that makes me want to avoid social situations altogether.

Do you ever feel certain that these appearance flaws are being deliberately caused or controlled by someone or something outside of you, or do you recognize they are a concern about your own appearance?

Oh no, I recognize these are entirely my own concerns about my own aging face, like my sagging skin and wrinkles. Nobody else is causing or controlling this; I am just deeply embarrassed and completely obsessed with how terrible I look under the lights.
Have you ever had this same kind of strong preoccupation with a specific body flaw or defect in the past, even when it was not related to social situations?

No, I've never experienced anything like this in the past. These feelings are actually very new to me and only started recently when I began planning my retirement and saw those photos from the birthday slideshow.
Do you also worry about being judged or embarrassed in social situations for reasons unrelated to your appearance, such as saying the wrong thing, blushing, or seeming awkward?
No, I don't really worry about things like saying the wrong thing or blushing. My anxiety and wanting to avoid people are purely focused on how terrible I look.

Do you ever avoid social situations mainly because you fear being judged, embarrassed, or awkward even when your appearance is not the focus, or is the problem only about the specific flaws you see in your appearance?

The problem is entirely about the specific flaws in my appearance. I don't fear social situations because of being awkward or judged on my personality; I am just deeply ashamed of how saggy, crooked, and wrinkled my face looks under the lights. I only avoid people because I'm terrified they will notice these exact flaws.

When you look in the mirror or at photos, do you spend a lot of time checking, comparing, or trying to hide these specific appearance flaws, or is your main problem only fear of being judged in social situations?

Yes, I spend an exhausting amount of time checking and trying to fix how I look. I'll stand inches from the bathroom mirror for hours tilting my head, smoothing my skin, and taking dozens of selfies just to zoom in on my wrinkles before begging my husband or sister to tell me if my face looks lopsided. It is an incredibly embarrassing cycle, but I just can't seem to stop doing it.
Do you feel that other people can clearly see a specific flaw in your appearance, or is the main fear that they will judge you even if they don’t notice any particular flaw?

I am absolutely convinced that other people can clearly see these specific flaws, like my saggy, crooked face and jawline under the lights. Even though my family and friends tell me they don't see anything wrong, I feel like it is incredibly obvious to everyone else and I'm deeply embarrassed by it.

When you are around people, is your main fear that they will judge you specifically because of your appearance flaws, or do you also fear being judged for social mistakes like saying the wrong thing, blushing, or seeming awkward even when your appearance is not the focus?

I'm not worried at all about saying the wrong thing or acting awkwardly in social situations. My fear is entirely about the shame of how my face, jawline, and neck look under the lights, and I am completely consumed by the terrifying thought that others are noticing those specific flaws.
Have you ever had any physical symptoms or medical tests related to these appearance concerns, or is the distress mainly about how your face looks and how others might see it?

No, I haven't had any physical symptoms or medical tests for this at all. The distress is entirely about how lopsided, saggy, and crooked my face looks to me, and the overwhelming fear and embarrassment that everyone else is noticing these flaws in photos or under bright lights.

Do you spend a lot of time worrying about a specific flaw in your appearance that you believe is real, or is your main fear being judged or embarrassed in social situations even when you are not focused on your appearance?

My worry is absolutely centered on the specific flaws in my appearance, like how saggy and crooked my jawline, neck, and wrinkles look under bright lights. Any fear I have of social situations is entirely because I am terrified of people noticing these specific physical flaws, rather than a general anxiety about socializing.
Have you ever had a long-standing fear of social situations because of being embarrassed, judged, or saying the wrong thing, even when you were not worried about your appearance?
No, I have never experienced a fear of social situations for reasons other than my appearance. My current anxiety and why I'm avoiding people are strictly tied to how terrible I look.
When you avoid people, is it only because of the specific flaws you see in your appearance, or do you also fear social situations in general even when your appearance is not on your mind?

My avoidance is entirely because of how terrible I think my face, jawline, and neck look under the lights. I don't have a general fear of social situations at all—in fact, I used to love choir and theater—but now I only stay home because I'm so ashamed of my appearance.

Do you ever worry that people are judging you in social situations for reasons unrelated to your appearance, such as being awkward, blushing, or saying the wrong thing, even when you are not focused on your face or body?

No, I don't worry about being awkward, blushing, or saying the wrong thing at all. My anxiety and social withdrawal are entirely focused on how saggy, crooked, and wrinkled my face looks under the lights. It is strictly about my appearance, not about how I behave in front of others.
Have you ever considered that these appearance flaws might be exaggerated or not actually visible to others, or are you completely certain they are real and obvious?

I am completely convinced that these flaws are real and glaringly obvious, especially under bright lights. My husband, sister, and friends all tell me they don't see anything wrong, but it is so hard to believe their reassurances when I look in the mirror or replay those photos in my head. To me, the saggy and crooked areas feel undeniably noticeable and deeply embarrassing.
Have you ever had these same concerns about a specific flaw in your appearance even when you were not in social situations, or do they only come up when you are around other people?

Yes, I absolutely have these concerns even when I am completely alone. I spend hours by myself in front of the bathroom mirror tilting my head, smoothing my skin, and taking selfies just to zoom in on my wrinkles and jawline. Even when there is no one else around, I just can't stop replaying those awful images of my face in my head.

When you are worried about going out, is your main fear that people will judge you because of a specific flaw in your appearance, or is it more that you will be embarrassed, awkward, or judged in social situations even if your appearance is not the focus?

It is absolutely about the specific flaws in my appearance, like my saggy jawline, crooked features, and deep wrinkles under the lights. I am not generally socially anxious or worried about being awkward at all. It is strictly the dread of people noticing and judging these physical flaws that makes me want to avoid others.
Do you ever think there is a chance that these appearance flaws might be exaggerated by your mind, or are you completely certain they are definitely real and obvious to everyone else?

I am completely certain they are real and obvious to everyone. Even though my husband and friends tell me they don't see anything, it is just too glaringly obvious under the lights for me to believe it's all in my mind. To me, the saggy and crooked parts of my face feel undeniably real.

Before these appearance concerns began, did you already feel anxious in social situations because of fear of being judged, embarrassed, or saying the wrong thing, even when you were not worried about your looks?

No, I don't think I ever felt that way before all of this started. I used to be very active in my community and genuinely enjoyed being around people. I never worried about being judged or embarrassed back then.

When you are avoiding people, is the main fear that they will judge you because of your appearance, or do you also fear being embarrassed or judged in social situations even when your appearance is not on your mind?

My fear is entirely centered on my appearance, and I don't worry about being judged or embarrassed for any other reasons. The dread of socializing and avoiding people is completely driven by my obsession over how terrible I look. I am just terrified that others are noticing my saggy, crooked face and wrinkles under the bright lights.
Do you ever think there is a chance that these appearance flaws might be exaggerated by your mind, or are you completely certain they are definitely real and obvious to everyone else?

Even though my husband and friends tell me they don't see anything, I just can't shake the conviction that these flaws are completely real and obvious to everyone. When I look in the mirror or see photos, the sagging and crookedness feel undeniably real and impossible to miss. It is just too glaringly obvious for me to believe it's something my mind is exaggerating.

Before these appearance concerns started, did you ever have a long-standing fear of social situations because of being judged, embarrassed, or saying the wrong thing, even when you were not worried about how you looked?
No, I don't think I ever had those kinds of fears before. I was always quite active and comfortable in my social groups until these appearance concerns started.

Do you avoid social situations mainly because you fear being judged for your appearance, or because you also fear being judged for things like blushing, sounding awkward, or saying the wrong thing even when your appearance is not the focus?

My avoidance is entirely because of how ashamed I am of my appearance, especially how my saggy jawline and wrinkles look under bright lights. I don't worry at all about blushing, sounding awkward, or saying the wrong thing in front of others. I am just completely consumed by embarrassment over how terrible my face looks, and that is the only reason I stay away.
